blocks.content: Minimum Support Price acts as a safety net for agricultural producers, insuring them against sharp dips in market prices during surplus production years.

rows: Announced prior to the sowing season
Announced at the start of the harvest season
Protect farmers from distress sales during bumper harvests
Procure foodgrains for the Public Distribution System and buffer stocks
Acts as a guaranteed floor price for farm produce
Historically set equal to or higher than MSP (currently merged with MSP)

items: CCEA (Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs) approves the MSP, whereas CACP only recommends it.
MSP covers 22 mandated crops (7 cereals, 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds, 3 commercial crops) plus FRP for Sugarcane.
Swaminathan Commission (NCF) recommended setting MSP at least 50% above the weighted average cost of production (C2 + 50%).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Food Corporation of India (FCI) was established under the Food Corporations Act 1964 to implement national food policy objectives.
Minimum Support Price (MSP) is a guaranteed price declared by the Government of India prior to the sowing season to protect farmers against steep price drops.
MSP recommendations are formulated by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) and approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA).
FCI carries out procurement, storage, transportation, and bulk distribution of foodgrains to support the Public Distribution System (PDS).
MSP calculation accounts for production costs including A2 (out-of-pocket costs), FL (family labor), and C2 (comprehensive cost including land rent and capital interest).
